name: How do you add natural light to a home office addition without overheating it?

mainEntity.name: What window and shading choices keep a Los Angeles office bright but comfortable in hot weather?
mainEntity.text: What window and shading choices keep a Los Angeles office bright but comfortable in hot weather?

acceptedAnswer.text: Natural light is one of the most requested features in a home office, but in Southern California it has to be balanced against heat and glare. The best approach is usually a combination of window placement, glazing choice, shading, and orientation. South- or west-facing glass may need stronger solar control, exterior shading, or interior coverings to avoid afternoon overheating. Clerestory windows, carefully sized openings, and thoughtful overhangs can bring in daylight while limiting direct sun. In a detached office, the building’s position on the lot can also influence how much glare and heat the room receives. Interior layout matters too, because a desk placed directly in front of a harsh window can make computer work uncomfortable. Homeowners should ask for a daylight plan, not just a window count, so the design supports both brightness and thermal comfort. The best office feels naturally lit without becoming a hot box in summer.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use windows that bring in daylight without excessive heat gain, then add shading, overhangs, or coverings to control afternoon sun. In Los Angeles, a bright office can still stay comfortable if glazing, orientation, and solar control are planned together.
